purpose: Candidate Engineering Assurance v0.3.2 adoption and the artifacts this repository consumes. Component versions are owned by its embedded matrix, not repeated here. The candidate remains withheld until the matrix has human acceptance and v0.3.2 is tagged.
matrix_authority: engineering-assurance compatibility native CLI at the exact v0.3.2 tag; scripts/check_shared_pins.py observes local tools and sends a versioned request. The CLI owns classification and the human-acceptance gate.
registry: Every npm component resolves from the public npm registry (registry.npmjs.org). The internal npm.ix mirror must not appear in any requirement, pin, lockfile, or .npmrc, and is not an oracle for whether a release landed. Querying an @agent-ix package needs --@agent-ix:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org; a bare --registry does not override the scoped .npmrc entry.

engineering_assurance.release_form: planned immutable git tag v0.3.2; candidate is not accepted or released

repinned_workflow_component.why: The hosted workflow pinned @agent-ix/quoin@0.22.5, which the packaged compatibility matrix names explicitly incompatible: it 'predates the `quoin change-assurance` surface; seal, intake, and receipt commands do not exist'. Every command this migration's chain runs is on that surface, so the old pin could not have worked. @agent-ix/ix-flow@0.0.4 was absent from the workflow entirely and is now installed.

repinned_ix_flow.why: TL-192 (mirrored from tl-mltl and tl-syntax): the packaged compatibility matrix authoritative for this repository's pin (matrix_authority above) classifies ix-flow strictly at the exact pinned version, so a locally-installed 0.2.3 against a v0.2.0 matrix pinning 0.0.4 classified as unknown, not compatible, and failed the local qualification gate. engineering-assurance v0.2.1 (release: accept ix-flow 0.2.3 matrix, agent-ix/engineering-assurance#47) re-pins the matrix to ix-flow 0.2.3 with human acceptance recorded (accepted_by Peter Krenesky, accepted_at 2026-09-10). This repository's engineering_assurance pin above moved from v0.2.0 to v0.2.1 in the same change so the workflow literal and the matrix authority agree; quire-cli and quoin stay at their already-accepted versions.

consumed_artifacts.why: Embedded in the exact native CLI. The CLI classifies its own reviewed matrix and reports human acceptance; no local version or digest rule is duplicated.

consumed_artifacts_note: Historical evidence artifacts remain deleted. Current classification uses the matrix embedded in the exact native EA CLI. This repository consumes no separate EA Python artifact.

upstream_dependency.why: The compiled pin is an exact reviewed tl-syntax commit, not a moving branch head. The advances from fed48a2f through 6d182fa9 to 9a4316e make the first-party license MIT-only and add syntax verification fixes and coverage tests; 9de638d adds an alloc-lane wrong-profile test only, and fca935e refreshes bounded V4 fuzz evidence only, without changing the parser-consumed production API; the earlier 4a561419 commit was tagged v0.3.0; Cargo.toml pins the current commit by rev, not by tag, so scripts/check_shared_pins.py can cross-check one literal across every file that names it, and the tl-syntax version requirement is =0.3.0 to match. The parser consumes its shared catalog and requirement-context types for the additive context-bound report, its future-operator lowering API for the clean-ascii v2 dialect, and its exported CORPUS_DIR constant to read the shared past-history corpus in place instead of vendoring a copy, while leaving the span-free semantic-identity family unconsumed. The authorship basis does not move: it is the revision whose bytes were read when this dialect was authored, and docs/ATTRIBUTION.md records both facts and the consumed/unconsumed delta separately. This pin field was last synchronized with Cargo.toml at agent-ix/tl-parse#32 (compiled_revision 8dc18eec) and silently drifted two pin bumps behind (#36 to e70f2379, #39 to 842d8255) before agent-ix/tl-parse TL-205/TL-204 caught and closed the gap. scripts/check_shared_pins.py (make pins) already cross-checks this field against Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, fuzz/Cargo.lock and src/lib.rs and would have failed loudly on that drift had it been run against it; TL-205 found the drift by git-history inspection instead.

known_drift: Resolved by the TL-192 bump to v0.2.1: engineering-assurance v0.2.0 packaged compatibility-matrix.json with accepted.state = pending_human_acceptance and shipped no human_acceptance_recorded predicate (agent-ix/engineering-assurance#20). v0.2.1 (release: accept ix-flow 0.2.3 matrix, #47) carries accepted.state = accepted with accepted_by and accepted_at populated, so the record this repository now reads is a real release carrying the acceptance rather than a branch head.

Historical: the human acceptance itself was never in doubt: Peter Krenesky accepted the FR-012 matrix on 2026-09-01, attributed on engineering-assurance main as ae50e13, and the pinned release now carries it (see above).

current_migration.note: Exact candidate pins for release prep. EA compatibility withholds until the named matrix acceptance is recorded and the immutable v0.3.2 tag exists. Historical migration records elsewhere in this file describe earlier releases.
